key_insight: Physically informed initialization helps origami optimization avoid basins that perform well continuously but fail after conversion to discrete hinge choices.
engineering_relevance: A stiff, flat hinge initialization bias improves discrete design success without additional compute or changes to the optimization process.
method: Use automatic differentiation in bilevel optimization to assign one of four hinge types to each fold on fixed-geometry sheets.
Bias initialization uniformly toward the stiff, flat hinge option before optimizing the continuous relaxation.
Alternatively, penalize geometric frustration and mechanical floppiness in the outer loss.
evidence_signal: Relaxed optimization solved 97% of runs, but discrete success was 49%; initialization bias raised it to 69%, while frustration and floppiness penalties raised it to 78%.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates gains on a specific origami design problem; transfer to other geometries or discrete mechanical systems remains unestablished.
paper_title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
